title: Token Evidence Sampling and SLO Assertion Runbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This runbook describes Redwood Inference’s standardized approach to token-level evidence sampling, SLO assertion at token granularity, and operational playbooks for investigating SLO regressions that are driven by inference workload characteristics (sequence length variability, quantization noise, cache-hit patterns). The goal is to enable high-fidelity SLO debugging without overwhelming telemetry storage and to provide a deterministic triage path when token-level signals are required for incident review or postmortem evidence.

Intended audience
- SREs owning model-serving SLOs and telemetry
- Runtime engineers implementing sampling hooks
- Observability/infra engineers operating metrics/trace pipelines
- Incident commanders (ICs) during degradation events

When to use this runbook
- P95/P99 latency, and token-error SLOs show unexplained drift
- Regression alerts that correlate with longer sequence length or higher KV-cache-miss rates
- Post-incident evidence requests from customers or compliance that require token-level context

Definitions and goals
- Token evidence: a compact per-request artifact capturing sequence length, per-token latencies (aggregated), model-variant id, quantization profile tag, KV-cache hit flag, and a short prompt-hash.
- Assertion window: time window used to evaluate an SLO (examples: 1h rolling, 7d rolling).
- Target SLOs for model-serving (examples; your service may vary):
  - Availability: successful responses >= 99.95 over 7d
  - Latency p99 (end-to-end): <= 400 ms for short-context (<=128 tokens) requests
  - Token-level processing latency p99: <= 8 ms/token

Telemetry strategy and sampling tiers
We operate three sampling tiers to balance signal and cost:

1) Baseline aggregate metrics (always-on)
- What: per-route counters and histograms (requests, errors, latency buckets, token-rate histograms, cache hit ratio).
- Retention: 90d for histograms and 365d for aggregated daily summaries.
- Purpose: produce SLO dashboards and alerts without token evidence.

2) Adaptive token sampling (targeted, 0.1%–5% global depending on load)
- Trigger conditions:
  - Rolling burn-rate > 0.5 (medium) OR
  - p99 latency breach on short-context route OR
  - Canary traffic during rollouts (all canary traffic sampled at 100%)
- What: per-request token evidence blob (compact JSON with per-token latency deciles, sequence length, model_variant, quant_profile, cache_flags, prompt-hash).
- Target global overhead: 0.5% of requests normal; adjustable by route and priority.
- Retention: 14d full token blobs; 180d summarized token deciles only.

3) Forensic capture (on-demand, 100% for targeted tenant/route during incident)
- Activated by an SRE runbook step or incident commander.
- What: full token traces including token-level logits snapshots for up to 1k tokens, request/response payloads (subject to privacy rules).
- Retention: 30d or as directed by incident/legal. Requires approval from Security for customer-sensitive data.

Sampling configuration examples
- Global adaptive sampling policy (YAML):

sampling_policy: |
  version: 2
  default_rate: 0.005                # 0.5% baseline
  triggers:
    - name: slo_burn_medium
      condition: burn_rate > 0.5
      rate: 0.02                    # 2% while burning
    - name: short_context_p99_breach
      condition: route_context == \"short\" AND latency_p99 > 400
      rate: 0.05
    - name: canary_all
      condition: traffic_tag == \"canary\"
      rate: 1.0
  max_storage_gb_per_day: 80

- Runtime toggle (CLI):
  rwoodctl telemetry sampling set --service model-runtime --policy-file /etc/telemetry/adaptive-sampling.yaml

Metric names and labels (canonical)
- inference.requests.count{route, tenant, model_variant}
- inference.responses.success{route, tenant} (boolean)
- inference.latency.ms.histogram{route,tenant,context_size_bucket}
- inference.token.latency.ms.quantiles{model_variant,quant_profile}  # token-level summaries
- inference.kv.cache_hit_ratio{model_variant,route}  # 0..1
- inference.token_evidence.captured{route,tenant,sampling_tier}

Alerting and SLO assertion examples
- Alert for p99 latency:
  - Expression (Grafana/PromQL-like):
    sum_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(inference.latency.ms.histogram[5m]))[1h:]) / ignoring() > 400
  - Initial IC action: check token sampling rate, routing failures, and cache-hit ratios. If adaptive sampling active, examine token evidence for last 1h.

- Burn-rate escalation thresholds and actions:
  1) burn_rate > 1.0 (critical): trigger high-priority incident, enable forensic capture for affected tenants, notify product and customer success.
  2) 0.5 < burn_rate <= 1.0 (warning): increase adaptive sampling rate to 5% for affected routes for 30 minutes and evaluate root-cause.

Runbook: step-by-step triage (p99 latency breach)
1) Initial evidence collection (0–5 minutes)
  - Verify alert source and timespan.
  - Confirm current sampling_policy: rwoodctl telemetry sampling get --service model-runtime
  - Pull aggregate metrics for the route: cpu, memory, qps, latency histograms, kv cache ratio.
  - If burn_rate > 0.5, set adaptive sampling rate to 2x default for 30m: rwoodctl telemetry sampling patch --route <route> --rate 0.02 --duration 30m
\2) Inspect token evidence (5–20 minutes)\  - Query recent token evidence blobs:
    ES query example: POST /_search?q=route:<route> AND @timestamp:[now-1h TO now]&size=100
  - Look for: sudden shift in median sequence length, percentile token latency skew (p95/p99 token latency increases), high cache-miss rate per request.
  - If token evidence shows consistent model_variant change, check rollout/traffic-routing config.
\3) Short fixes (20–60 minutes)\  - If a new model variant causes degradation: rollback to previous stable model and monitor.
    - rwoodctl model rollout rollback --route <route> --to-version <previous>
  - If cache-miss increase: restart KV-cache workers for the model shard (see KV-cache runbook) and monitor cache-hit metrics.
  - If quantization profile mismatch: pin requests to non-quantized variant and notify model-onboarding.
\4) Forensic (if needed)\  - If evidence insufficient, escalate to forensic capture: IC opens an incident board and requests Security approval if request payloads contain PII.
  - Enable forensic capture for tenant X: rwoodctl telemetry capture start --route <route> --tenant <tenant> --duration 2h --level forensic
\5) Post-incident evidence package and postmortem (post-incident)
  - Export token-evidence samples (CSV + summarized deciles) and attach to the incident.
  - Correlate with deployment timeline, autoscaler events, and cross-region routing decisions.
  - Make a concrete remediation: sampling tuning, SLO adjustment, model rollback, autoscaler tuning, or failover rules.

Privacy and retention controls
- Token evidence may contain prompt hashes only; do not store full prompt or response payloads except under forensic capture with explicit approval.
- Redact or hash any PII before indexing. The telemetry pipeline will run the redaction filter prior to storage:
  - redaction.enabled: true
  - redaction.rules: [prompt_hashing, ip_masking]

Ownership and SLAs for evidence requests
- Telemetry engineering team owns sampling platform.
- On-call SREs own immediate triage and enabling adaptive sampling during incidents.
- Forensic capture approvals are coordinated with Security and Legal for customer-sensitive requests.
- Evidence request SLA: 48 business hours for a signed customer evidence package (longer if legal review required).

Operational caveats and trade-offs
- Sampling biases: adaptive triggers can over-sample failing tenants. Always verify global and per-tenant sampling rates before drawing conclusions.
- Storage budget: keep global max_storage_gb_per_day and enforce alerting when > 80% capacity.
- Performance impact: token evidence capture should add <5% p95 latency; run regular performance benchmarks when changing capture format.

Dashboards and queries to inspect
- Dashboard: \"Token Evidence Health\" (Panels)
  - Global sampling rate over time
  - token.latency.deciles by model_variant and quant_profile
  - Cache-hit ratio and token-evidence capture events timeline
  - Forensic capture active flags per-tenant
\\- Example Elasticsearch aggregation for token p95 by model_variant (pseudo-DSL):
  {
    \"size\":0,
    \"aggs\":{
      \"by_variant\":{
        \"terms\":{\"field\":\"model_variant\"},
        \"aggs\":{
          \"p95_token_latency\":{
            \"percentiles\":{\"field\":\"token_latency_ms\",\"percents\":[95]}
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }

Change control and rollout guidance
- Any sampling policy change that modifies default_rate or max_storage must be reviewed by Observability and SRE leads.
- Roll out changes to sampling_policy gradually via canary: enable new policy for low-traffic route for 24h, validate storage/latency impact, then expand.

Known limitations
- Token evidence is not a substitute for model internals debugging (logits/time-sliced internals). Use forensic capture in those cases.
- Long-tail (rare) requests may still be missed by sampling; tune adaptive triggers accordingly.

Appendix A: Example token evidence blob (compact)
{
  \"request_id\": \"r-34a7\",
  \"timestamp\": \"2026-07-14T13:24:12Z\",
  \"route\": \"chat-short\",
  \"model_variant\": \"gptx-13b-q4\",
  \"quant_profile\": \"q4_8bit\",
  \"sequence_length\": 96,
  \"token_latency_deciles_ms\": [1.0,1.2,1.3,1.4,1.7,2.1,3.8,5.4,7.6,12.0],
  \"kv_cache_hit\": false,
  \"prompt_hash\": \"sha256:ab12...\"
}

Appendix B: Escalation contacts
- Telemetry engineering (pager): #telemetry-oncall
- Model runtime oncall: #model-runtime-oncall
- Security (approval for forensic): security-approvals@redwood.ai
